info.desc: Fully Completely is the third studio album by Canadian rock band The Tragically Hip. The album was released in October 1992 and produced by Chris Tsangarides. The album produced six singles: "Locked in the Trunk of a Car", "Fifty Mission Cap", "Courage (For Hugh MacLennan)", "At the Hundredth Meridian", "Looking for a Place to Happen", and "Fully Completely". .

podcast.body: Released in 1992, this album is regarded by some as The Tragically Hip's best work, serving as an extensive lesson in Canadian history and geography. It weaves together references to historical figures, political events, and geographical locations across Canada. "After road apples came what is probably the best tragically hip album, fully completely in 1992."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released on October 6, 1992, this album was recorded at Battery Studios in Willesden Green, North London, in July 1992, produced by Chris Sangerides. It marked a departure from the band's usual live-recording style, with Sangerides building tracks from the ground up, starting with bass and drums for the first three weeks. This method contributed to a "bigger sound," more instrument isolation, and enhanced guitar sounds. The album immediately sold 140,000 copies in Canada upon release, reaching 200,000 within three months, and by January 2007, it was certified for over 1 million domestic sales (a diamond award), placing it in company with albums like U2's *Joshua Tree* and Nirvana's *Nevermind*. It was the only Hip album to be released in Japan, on April 23, 1993. A 2014 Deluxe Reissue included a remastered album, two bonus tracks, and a complete live recording from an invitation-only record release show at the Horseshoe Tavern on September 13, 1992. "they had no idea that they had created something extraordinary."
